subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the Windows PowerShell smoke lane include `pnpm build:strict-smoke` now, or start with a narrower passing command set?
rationale: The source path is clear, but selecting recurring Windows CI work and whether to include the currently failing build smoke needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Fix full command set first
options.body: Keep `pnpm check:docs` and `pnpm build:strict-smoke`, but land only after the Windows `pwsh` lane passes with proof.

options.title: Land narrower smoke first
options.body: Start with the native PowerShell commands that already pass and track build-smoke coverage separately.

options.title: Defer recurring Windows smoke
options.body: Keep the issue open until runner budget and Windows build-smoke ownership are settled.

recommendation.title: Fix full command set first
recommendation.body: Keep `pnpm check:docs` and `pnpm build:strict-smoke`, but land only after the Windows `pwsh` lane passes with proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent overlap across CI workflow maintenance and PowerShell-safe docs tooling.
